question.problem:
For the function $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, you're given the following data:

$$
f(-2)=-3,\,{f}^{′}(-2)=\frac{1}{2},\,g(-2)=4,\,{g}^{′}(-2)=-2
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=-2.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=-2}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x)) & =f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where $x=-2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=-2} & =f(-2){g}^{′}(-2)+g(-2){f}^{′}(-2) \\  & =(-3)\cdot (-2)+4\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
